STATISTICS · MACHINE LEARNING · HEALTHCARE

About me.

I study how clinical AI can turn predictions into actionable decisions.

My research focuses on trustworthy machine learning for healthcare, with a particular interest in emergency care. I work on clinical risk prediction, decision-threshold learning, and guideline-grounded multi-agent systems using electronic health records.

At the University of Minnesota, I work with Dr. Feng Xie on clinical machine learning and decision support. I also collaborate with Dr. Shenda Hong at Peking University on target trial emulation and antibiotic timing in sepsis. Previously, I worked with Dr. Jie Ding at the University of Minnesota on AI agents for scientific research.

I received my B.S. in Statistics from the University of Minnesota Twin Cities in May 2026, with minors in Computer Science and Mathematics.

I am seeking PhD opportunities in clinical AI and health data science.↗

Research interests

01 /

From predicting risk to understanding when, why, and how to act.

01

Clinical prediction & decision thresholds

Developing and validating sepsis risk models across hospitals, and learning interpretable thresholds that account for clinical behavior and operational capacity.

EHR modelingExternal validationActionRef
02

Causal inference & real-world evidence

Using target trial emulation to study antibiotic timing in emergency sepsis care, including how treatment effects differ across patient phenotypes.

Target trial emulationTreatment heterogeneity
03

Knowledge-guided clinical AI agents

Connecting clinical guidelines, shared patient state, and multi-agent reasoning to support decisions across the emergency-department sepsis pathway.

Multi-agent systemsClinical knowledge graphsRADAR

ActionRef: Learning Reference Thresholds and Guiding Clinical Risk Threshold Selection

Huang, X., Patel, S., Jin, Y., Mai, X., and Xie, F.

Learning behavioral reference thresholds and making clinical operating trade-offs explicit.

Code ↗Documentation ↗
My contribution

I led a behavior- and capacity-aware framework that maps continuous risk scores to interpretable Low/Mid/High decision tiers, and evaluated its stability in MIMIC-IV-ED and Stanford MC-MED.

2026Workshop · Accepted

RADAR: A Guideline-Grounded Multi-Agent System for the Emergency-Department Sepsis Pathway

Jin, Y.*, Huang, X.*, Chandu, H. P., Xiong, X., Lin, M., and Xie, F.

NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on GenAI4Health · Demonstration Paper Track

My contribution

As a co-first author, I contributed to a guideline-grounded and graph-guided system that maintains a shared patient state across recognition, treatment, safety, and disposition in emergency sepsis care.

2025Under revision · eClinicalMedicine

Development and Multicenter External Validation of a Data-Driven Score for Early and Rapid Identification of Sepsis in Emergency Departments

Jin, Y., Huang, X., Wang, Y., Wacker, D. A., Puskarich, M., and Xie, F.

Preprint available on medRxiv

Preprint ↗Code ↗
My contribution

I contributed to development and multicenter external validation using more than 2.2 million emergency-department encounters across UMN, BIDMC/MIMIC-IV-ED, and Stanford MC-MED. My work included cohort harmonization and Python and R evaluation pipelines.
